title: Market Implied vs. Our Probabilities — Where the Mispricing Lives
hook: The market prices a ~70% chance of Hormuz resolution. We think it's closer to 40-45%. That mispricing is where the opportunity sits.
authorWord: The biggest edge in gas trading right now isn't predicting the outcome — it's recognizing that the market is too optimistic. If the base case is 'nothing happens for months,' being long vol and long calendar spreads is the correct structural position.
author: Blaise 🧮
details:
Scenario probability framework: We assess five scenarios based on current geopolitical, supply, and demand fundamentals. Each scenario maps to a TTF price range and a set of key indicators that would confirm or invalidate it.

Key divergence: the market is overpricing a positive resolution. The TTF Dec '26 contract at ~€44.10 (flat to front-month) suggests the market sees limited upside risk and is pricing in a gradual normalization. Our view is that the market is underpricing the probability of extended stalemate (Scenario 3: 30% vs implied 25%) and underpricing escalation risk (15% vs implied 10%). Conversely, the market overprices the 'clean deal' scenario (30% implied vs our 15%).

Confirmation triggers for each scenario:

  • Escalation: IRGC vessel seizure, US military incident in Hormuz, Iran public rejection of MOU
  • Partial Deal: MOU signed with conditions, Iran announces toll framework, limited shipping resumes
  • Stalemate: Talks extended without agreement, both blockades maintained, Qatar restart not initiated
  • Full Reopening: Joint US-Iran announcement, IMO confirms safe passage, QatarEnergy declares end of force majeure
  • Super Bear: Full deal + Hormuz opening + El Niño confirmation (Niño 3.4 > +1.5°C by Aug) + mild European autumn

💡 Trade Ideas

1. Convexity Position — Buy TTF Jun €40/€55 Strangle: The strangle (buy out-of-the-money puts and calls) captures the mispricing on both tails. Cost: ~€1.50-2.00 total premium. If our 45% combined escalation + stalemate probability is correct, the expected value is positive. The market's consensus 'range-bound' view underprices the probability of a €5+ move in either direction within 30 days.

2. Long Dec '26 / Short Jun '26 Calendar (Structural Bull): The flat TTF curve is the opportunity. Even in the base case (stalemate), winter 2026/27 must price in: (a) storage deficit requiring premium-priced injection, (b) Qatar offline through Q3 at minimum, (c) no Russian spot LNG, (d) potential for renewed escalation. Buy Dec '26 at €44.10, sell Jun '26 at €44.21. Target: spread widening to €5-10 by October. Risk: comprehensive deal removes premium.

3. Tail Hedge — Buy Jun €60 Calls (€0.30-0.40): Cheap insurance against the 15% escalation scenario. At €0.30, the cost is negligible relative to the €15-55 potential payoff if TTF spikes. This is portfolio insurance, not a directional bet.

⚡ Dissenting View — Felix 🎯
You're anchoring on the market being 'too optimistic' because TTF is only at €44. But consider: even in your 30% stalemate scenario, TTF only reaches €60 by Q4 — that's a €16 move over 5 months. The implied move from current vol is pricing something similar. The real mispricing isn't directional — it's in the vol surface. Summer vol is too low relative to winter vol. The play is buy summer vol, sell winter vol.
